Week | Deliverable | Exit check |

Gate. An uncoached player can state the objective and fail conditions, pick an approach because of something they learned, explain its cash, time and Trail cost, complete a chain, say why they fought police rather than rivals (or the reverse), and read what the next mission inherits.
If the schedule slips, cut in this order: crowd witnesses (crowds stay decorative) → patrol reroute → camera-block variant → the police branch of the final fight (rivals only). Always keep both routes, the one payoff cut, the debrief and the gate test.

§14 ROLES › Keel
### Keel · Simulation engineer · Opus 5.5
owns: The rulebook: every event in the city, what it needs, what it changes and who sees it. Also the 28 test scenarios and the C# sim library that runs them (Unity-free; provisional, Sky to confirm).
receives: Motive's rules, Waymark's missions, Pulse's schedules, Fable's lines, and what the debrief carries forward.
delivers: The rulebook to everyone; checked content to Latch; mistakes back to their authors. Design decisions stay with Motive.
hold: The rules live apart from the engine. Any run replays exactly from its starting state and the player's orders. One incident counts once toward Alert and dispatches once. Silent acts raise Alert when the report lands. Unity must pass the same 28 scenarios before content goes in. One C# engine: Unity runs it live, tools headless via dotnet; 10 Hz, integer state, replay = orders + checksums. Locked only after the week 4 playtest.

§14 ROLES › Redline
### Redline · Code and performance reviewer · Opus 5.5
owns: Code review and performance.
receives: Latch's build and the performance targets.
delivers: A review. Latch fixes; Redline retests.
hold: Judge by frame rate at play zoom, not polygon counts: 60 fps at 1080p on a 15-inch MacBook Air M4 (Mac16,13; the reference machine: no fan, 10-core GPU), measured warm at play zoom with people, vehicles and the simulation in, by a perf harness in a development build; a mid-range PC (RTX 3060-class GPU, 6-core CPU) must also pass, as a check. 30 active combatants at most; the background crowd can be far larger (a 10,000-citizen stress test already runs). Anything that breaks exact replay is a defect.

One lead, clear owners, named handoffs › Decisions (v0.17.0)
Budget. Agent work runs inside two existing 20× subscriptions (one Codex, one Claude), which cap usage over time rather than charging per use. Aster watches both and drops optional work when the allowance runs low. Anything paid per use, such as Runware and Meshy credits, is priced before use.
Review record and version history: ../the-suborned-gdd-changelog.html . The Suborned · Game Design Document v0.24.0 · Sky Rumsey · 18 October 2026. Rules tagged Built come from docs/prototypes/suborned-world-sim.js . Values tagged Spec are starting points to be tuned against playtests.

Nothing hand-authored, everything checked
Consequences | The rules, applied to the mission log | Replaying the mission to confirm the same result |
The mission checker: a generated mission ships only if at least 2 quiet routes win · a loud route exists and costs more Trail · every way to fail can actually happen · no single contact is essential · a player who knows everything finishes with at least a minute to spare. An open case counts as 3 Trail.
The risk is sameness. When everyone is generated, it's easy for nobody to be memorable. Watch Dogs: Legion is the cautionary example. The answer is history, not backstory : people become memorable through what the systems record with you (who you helped, who got braver, who sold you out). Generated text is only a light layer on top. Every fact a person carries must change a price or an outcome: a field that no rule reads is rejected, because detailed bios that change nothing (Legion again) are the opposite of memorable.

§08 CAMPAIGN › objectives
objectives [S]: kidnapping · bank job via planted teller · killing by manipulated proxy · takeover via ruined reputation. Direct force always works, with bigger T.
debrief [B] → next mission:
| output | states | from |
| public security | Calm → Raised → High | final A; any shot fired |
| investigation | little → early → active (named cause) | T 0 / 1–2 / 3+; named witnesses take precedence |
| assets | e.g. Inez introduces café contacts; Inez may identify Fixer | how turned, what they saw |
| standing [S] | one line per district: band, number, change and its cause ("Harbour: Hero +3 ▲1, Inez told her family a stranger cleared her debt") | acts seen or found, public fights, word of mouth, drift (§04) |
| missing persons and cases [S] | each open case; the area watch: +1 posted guard and +1 camera on the block where the person was last seen, for 3 missions; the district's security level S | a kill never found: +2 T, no Menace, close ties fear +1, the case stays open until the body is found · a found killing: −1 Standing, grief, its case closes after 3 missions · every 2 open cases raise S by 1, at most +2 |
| statements [S] | knockout victims who came home: +4 T and their facts as leads (the face if they saw it coming) | knockouts not quieted |
| bravery, resentment, Heat [S] | per contact / campaign | jobs, pressure used, grief and worry |
